title: Amygdala astrocyte primary cilium mechanisms contribute to stress behaviours.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Fetched GEO SuperSeries GSE285150 (public Jun 2026): 98 mouse samples split across 8 sub-series (GSE285145 n=8, GSE285147 n=23, GSE285148 n=16, GSE285149 n=16, GSE326592 n=8, GSE326595 n=7, GSE326603 n=8, GSE326646 n=12), each with one processed xlsx. Downloaded GSE285147_ProcessedData_set2.xlsx (6.0 MB): one sheet of raw read counts, 48,795 Ensembl mouse genes x 23 sample columns (e.g. AMY_CRS_COM_1, AMY_CRS_IP_1), condition encoded only in column names. GEO design text says 4 mice were pooled per sample.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Proteomics in MassIVE MSV000096647 (not opened); DEG (differentially expressed gene) lists and behaviour source data in Nature supplement (Europe PMC supplement listing timed out, not retrieved); reuse of 13-region astrocyte data GSE198024 (not opened).

a1_downloadable.note: GEO processed xlsx files download openly; checked one (6.0 MB).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No label column: condition (stress vs control, IP vs input, genotype) is encoded only in sample column names, and any gene-level label (differential expression) would have to be computed from the counts. Checked in the set2 file.

a3_inputs_present.note: Gene counts with Ensembl IDs present in the file.

a4_units_stated.note: Raw read counts (integers), sheet named metaReadCount.

a5_enough_rows.note: 98 bulk RNA-seq samples total across 8 differently designed experiments (largest one has 23), each sample pooling 4 mice; far below the ~400 minimum for classification. Counted from GEO.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO sub-series sizes sum to 98; did not cross-check per-experiment n against paper figures.

a8_label_provenance.note: Treating genes as rows, the only labels (DEG status or fold change) are derived from these same counts by limma-voom (a statistical tool for differential expression), so the label is computed from the features.

backbone.name: Geneformer (a single-cell gene expression model) would be the nearest match, but the data is pooled bulk RNA-seq

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which astrocyte genes respond to stress specifically in the amygdala? That is a differential-expression question, not one a model needs to answer.

controls.positive_control: Astrocyte markers (Aldh1l1, Gfap) enriched in Ribotag IP (pulled-down astrocyte RNA) versus input samples.
controls.external_validation: None at sample level; other stress RNA-seq atlases exist but use different cell types and protocols.

honest_claim_h3: With 8 to 23 pooled samples per experiment, a model could at most separate stressed from control amygdala astrocyte samples within one experiment. That is a differential-expression result, not a generalisable predictor.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use astrocyte gene expression from the mouse amygdala to predict whether the animal underwent chronic stress.
plain_idea.train_on: Read counts for 48,795 genes per sample. There are 98 samples in total across 8 experiments, each sample pooled from 4 mice.
plain_idea.predict: Stress or control (or genotype) group, which is set by the experimental design and recorded only in sample names.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Little. With this few samples, differential expression already answers the question, and a classifier would mostly learn the batch.

ml_idea: Sample-level classification of stress status from astrocyte transcriptomes. It is not viable: 98 pooled samples across 8 heterogeneous experiments, and gene-level labels would be computed from the same counts.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the 6 MB set2 file size; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count samples in GEO: 98 total, the largest experiment 23. Done, and it kills the project.

verdict_reason: A5/A2/A8 fail. The open data is 98 pooled mouse bulk RNA-seq samples across 8 differently designed experiments, with condition only in column names, and any gene-level label would be computed from the same counts. This is a mechanistic experimental paper with no model-sized dataset.
